en: Melting uses heat to change a solid like butter into a liquid, whereas dissolving mixes a solid like sugar into a liquid solvent like water.
Evaporation happens at any temperature when surface molecules of liquid water gain enough energy to become gas, not just at the boiling point.
Air is a mixture of gases that has mass and takes up space, which is why a basketball becomes heavier when pumped full of air.
Rusting is a chemical change where iron reacts with oxygen and water to form a completely new substance called iron oxide, not just surface dirt.
Water expands and becomes less dense when it freezes into solid ice, which is why ice cubes float on top of liquid water in a glass.
Boiling liquid water into steam is a physical change because the molecules remain H2O and can condense back into liquid water without forming a new substance.
Pure liquid water is a chemical compound, not a solution, because its hydrogen and oxygen atoms are chemically bonded rather than just physically mixed.
Melted chocolate remains chocolate because melting is a reversible physical change that alters its state without creating any new chemical substances.
Sand mixed in water forms a heterogeneous mixture, not a solution, because the solid sand particles do not dissolve and will eventually settle at the bottom.
Burning wood is an irreversible chemical change that produces entirely new substances like ash, carbon dioxide gas, and water vapor, rather than just changing its shape.
Water droplets on a cold juice glass come from water vapor in the warm outside air cooling and condensing into liquid, not from liquid leaking through the glass.
Solid dry ice undergoes sublimation to become carbon dioxide gas directly, skipping the liquid state entirely when exposed to room temperature.
